content_sanskrit: अथ प्रपेदे त्रिदशैरशेषैः क्रूरासुरोपप्लवदुःखितात्मा । पुलोमपुत्रीदयितोऽन्धकारिं पत्त्रीव तृष्णातुरितः पयोदम् ॥

meaning_english: Then Indra, the beloved of Śacī, whose mind was distressed by the harassment caused by cruel demons, approached Lord Śiva (the enemy of Andhaka) accompanied by all the gods, just as a thirsty bird approaches a rain-bearing cloud.

content_sanskrit: दृप्तारिसन्त्रासखिलीकृतात्स कथञ्चिदम्भोदविहारमार्गात् । अवातताराभिगिरिं गिरीशगौरीपदन्यासविशुद्धमिन्द्रः ॥

meaning_english: Indra somehow descended from the celestial path through the clouds—a path he had rendered unused out of fear of his arrogant enemies—toward the mountain Kailāsa, which was sanctified by the footprints of Lord Śiva and Goddess Pārvatī.

content_sanskrit: सङ्क्रन्दनः स्यन्दनतोऽवतीर्य मेघात्मनो मातलिदत्तहस्तः । पिनाकिनोऽथालयमुच्चचाल शुचौपिपासाकुलितो यथाम्भः ॥

meaning_english: Then Indra, leaning on the hand of his charioteer Mātali, descended from his chariot and proceeded toward the abode of Lord Śiva, who is of the nature of a cloud. He resembled a person parched by thirst in summer moving toward water.

content_sanskrit: इतस्ततोऽथ प्रतिबिम्बभाजं विलोकमानः स्फटिकाद्रिभूमौ । आत्मानमप्येकमनेकधा स व्रजन्विभोरास्पदमाससाद ॥

meaning_english: As he walked, Indra saw his single self reflected many times in the crystal ground of the mountain. Observing himself thus multiplied, he reached the residence of the Lord Śiva.

content_sanskrit: विचित्रचञ्चन्मणिभङ्गिसङ्गं सौवर्णदण्डं दधतातिचण्डम् । स नन्दिनाधिष्ठितमध्यतिष्ठत्सौधाङ्गणद्वारमनङ्गशत्रोः ॥

meaning_english: He reached the gate of the palace courtyard of Lord Śiva, which was guarded by the fierce Nandin. Nandin held a golden staff adorned with an array of various sparkling gems.

content_sanskrit: ततः स कक्षाहितहेमदण्डो नन्दी सुरेन्द्रं प्रतिपद्य सद्यः । प्रतोषयामास सुगौरवेण गत्वा शशंस स्वयमीश्वरस्य ॥

meaning_english: Then Nandin, placing his golden staff under his arm, approached Indra and immediately welcomed him with great respect. Afterward, he went in person and announced Indra's arrival to Lord Śiva.

content_sanskrit: भ्रूसंज्ञयानेन कृताभ्यनुज्ञः सुरेश्वरं तं जगदीश्वरेण । प्रवेशयामास सुरैः पुरोगः समं स नन्दी सदनं सदस्य ॥

meaning_english: Having received a command from Lord Śiva through a mere movement of his eyebrow, Nandin led the way and escorted Indra, along with the other gods, into the assembly hall of the Lord of the Universe.

content_sanskrit: स चण्डिभृङ्गिप्रमुखैर्गरिष्ठैर्गणैरनेकैर्विविधस्वरुपैः । अधिष्ठितं संसदि रत्नमय्यां सहस्रनेत्रः शिवमालुलोके ॥

meaning_english: The thousand-eyed Indra beheld Lord Śiva in a gem-studded assembly hall. The Lord was surrounded by numerous venerable Gaṇas of various forms, led by prominent figures such as Caṇḍī and Bhṛṅgin.

content_sanskrit: कपर्दमुद्बद्धमहीनमूर्धरत्नांशुभिर्भासुरमुल्लसद्भिः । दधानमुच्चैस्तरमिद्धधातोः सुमेरुशृङ्गस्य समत्वमाप्तम् ॥

meaning_english: He saw Śiva wearing matted hair tied up high, which was brilliant with the glistening rays of gems from the heads of serpents. His hair attained a likeness to the lofty peak of Mount Sumeru, which is rich with glowing minerals.

content_sanskrit: बिभ्राणमुत्तुङ्गतरङ्गमालां गङ्गां जटाजूटतटं भजन्तीम् । गौरीं तदुत्सङ्गजुषं हसन्तीमिव स्वफेनैः शरदभ्रशुभ्रैः ॥

meaning_english: He saw the Lord bearing the river Ganges, which was flowing over his matted hair with high waves. The Ganges, with her foam as white as autumn clouds, seemed to be laughing at Goddess Pārvatī, who was seated on the Lord’s lap.

content_sanskrit: गङ्गातरङ्गप्रतिबिम्बितैः स्वैर्बहूभवन्तं शिरसा सुधांशुम् । चलन्मरीचिप्रचयैस्तुषारगौरैर्हिमद्योतितमुद्वहन्तम् ॥

meaning_english: Lord Śiva is described bearing the moon on his head. Due to the reflections in the waves of the Gaṅgā, the single moon appears to have become manifold. The moon, white as frost, shines with clusters of moving rays, illuminating the Lord's head as he carries it.

content_sanskrit: भालस्थले लोचनमेधमानधामाधरीभूतरवीन्दुनेत्रम् । युगान्तकालोचितहव्यवाहं मीनध्वजप्लोषणमादधानम् ॥

meaning_english: Śiva possesses a third eye on his forehead with increasing radiance that surpasses the brilliance of his other two eyes (the sun and moon). This eye, which consumed Kāmadeva, glows like the cataclysmic fire that appears at the end of a Yuga.

content_sanskrit: महार्हरत्नाञ्चितयो रुदारं स्फुरत्प्रभामण्डलयोः समन्तात् । कर्णस्थिताभ्यां शशिभास्कराभ्यामुपासितं कुण्डलयोश्छलेन ॥

meaning_english: Lord Śiva appears as if being worshipped or attended by the sun and the moon themselves, who have taken the form of his two magnificent earrings. These earrings are adorned with precious gems and cast a wide halo of brilliant light from his ears.

content_sanskrit: स्वबद्धया कण्ठिकयेव नीलमाणिक्यमय्या कुतुकेन गौर्याः । नीलस्य कण्ठस्य परिस्फुरन्त्या कान्त्या महत्या सुविराजमानम् ॥

meaning_english: The Lord shines beautifully due to the great radiating luster of his blue throat. It appears as if Gaurī, out of playful curiosity, has tied a necklace made of blue sapphires around his neck.

content_sanskrit: कालार्दितानां त्रिदशासुराणां चितारजोभिः परिपाण्डुरङ्गम् । महन्महेभाजिनमुद्गताभ्रप्रालेयशैलश्रियमुद्वहन्तम् ॥

meaning_english: Lord Śiva's body is smeared white with the funeral ashes of gods and demons destroyed by Time. Wearing the hide of a great elephant, he possesses the majestic beauty of the snowy Himālaya mountains capped by rising clouds.

content_sanskrit: पाणिस्थितब्रह्मकपालपात्रं वैकुण्ठभाजापि निषेध्यमाणाम् । नरास्थिखण्डाभरणं रणान्तमूलं त्रिशूलं कलयन्तमुच्चैः ॥

meaning_english: Wielding his trident high—the weapon that ends all battles—Śiva holds a skull-bowl in his hand. He is adorned with ornaments of human bone fragments, a sight so formidable that even Viṣṇu attempts to avert it.

content_sanskrit: पुरातनीं ब्रह्मकपालमालां कण्ठे वहन्तं पुनराश्वसन्तीम् । उद्गीतवेदां मुकुटेन्दुवर्षत्सुधा भरौघाप्लवलब्धसंज्ञाम् ॥

meaning_english: On his neck, Śiva wears an ancient garland of skulls. These skulls have regained consciousness and are breathing again, even chanting the Vedas, because they are constantly bathed in the overflowing nectar raining down from the moon on Śiva's crown.

content_sanskrit: सलीलमङ्कस्थितया गिरीन्द्रपुत्र्या नवाष्टापदवल्लिभासा । विराजमानं शरदभ्रखण्डं परिस्फुरन्त्याचिररोचिषेव ॥

meaning_english: Lord Śiva shines while Pārvatī sits gracefully on his lap. With her complexion like a fresh golden creeper, she resembles a flash of lightning illuminating a white autumnal cloud, which is represented by the ash-smeared Lord.

content_sanskrit: दृप्ताऽन्धकप्राणहरं पिनाकं महासुरस्त्रीविधवत्वहेतुम् । करेण गृह्णान्तमगृह्यमन्यैः पुरास्मरप्लोषणकेलिकारम् ॥

meaning_english: With his hand, Śiva grasps the Pināka bow, which cannot be wielded by anyone else. This is the same Lord who playfully burnt Kāmadeva in the past, slew the arrogant demon Andhaka, and brought widowhood to the wives of the great demons.

content_sanskrit: भद्रासनं काञ्चनपादपीठं महार्हमाणिक्यविभङ्गिचित्रम् । अधिष्ठितं चन्द्रमरीचिगौरैरुद्वीज्यमानं चमरैर्गणाभ्याम् ॥

meaning_english: Lord Śiva is seated upon an auspicious throne that features a golden footstool and is beautifully inlaid with precious rubies. He is being fanned by two of his attendants using fly-whisks as white as the rays of the moon.

content_sanskrit: शस्त्रास्त्रविद्याभ्यसनैकसक्ते सविस्मयैरेत्य गणैः सुदृष्टे । नीराज्यमाने स्फटिकाचलेन सानन्दनिर्दिष्टदृशं कुमारे ॥

meaning_english: While Kumāra was intently practiced in the science of arms, the amazed Gaṇas approached and gazed at him. As the crystal mountain Kailāsa seemed to perform a lustration ritual for him with its radiance, Śiva cast his joyful eyes upon his son.

content_sanskrit: तथाविधं शैलसुताधिनाथं पुलोमपुत्रीदयितो निरीक्ष्य । आसीत्क्षणं क्षोभपरो नु कस्य मनो न हि क्षुभ्यति धामधाम्नि ॥

meaning_english: Upon seeing the Lord of Pārvatī in such a majestic state, Indra, the husband of Śacī, became momentarily overwhelmed with emotion. Indeed, whose mind would not be stirred when standing before the most brilliant and supreme radiance?

content_sanskrit: विकरस्वराभ्भोजवनश्रिया तं दृशं सहस्रेण निरीक्षमाणः । रोमालिभिः स्वर्गपतिर्बभासे पुष्पोत्कराकीर्ण इवाम्रशाखी ॥

meaning_english: Indra, beholding Śiva with his thousand eyes that resembled a forest of blooming lotuses, shone brilliantly. With his hair standing on end due to devotion, he looked like a mango tree covered in clusters of blossoms.

content_sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा सहस्रेण दृशां महेशमभूत्कृतार्थोऽतितरां महेन्द्रः । सर्वाङ्गजातं तदथो विरुपमिव प्रियाकोपकरं विवेद ॥

meaning_english: Having beheld Lord Śiva with his thousand eyes, Indra felt immensely fulfilled. However, he then reflected upon those many eyes covering his body, which usually caused his wife Śacī's anger, and for a moment considered them a deformity.

content_sanskrit: ततः कुमारं कनकाद्रिसारं पुरन्दरः प्रेक्ष्य धृतास्त्रशस्त्रम् । महेश्वरोपान्तिकवर्तमानं शत्रोर्जयाशां मनसा बबन्ध ॥

meaning_english: Then Indra, seeing Kumāra standing near Maheśvara, equipped with weapons and possessing the strength of Mount Meru, finally felt a firm hope in his heart for victory over his enemy.

content_sanskrit: श्रीनीलकण्ठ द्युपतिः पुरोऽस्ति त्वयि प्रणामावसरं प्रतीच्छन् । सहस्रनेत्रेऽत्र भव त्रिनेत्र दृष्ट्या प्रसाद प्रगुणो महेश ॥

meaning_english: Nandi addressed Śiva: 'O illustrious Blue-throated Lord, the King of Heaven stands before you, seeking an opportunity to prostrate. O Three-eyed Lord, please look upon this thousand-eyed Indra with a favorable and gracious gaze.'

meaning_english: Thus, with folded hands, Nandi approached and placed his golden staff under his arm. Seeking to remain a recipient of Śiva's grace, he then spoke these words to the enemy of Smara (Śiva).

meaning_english: Then the enemy of Tripura, who is served by all three worlds, cast a gracious glance upon Indra, who is served by the gods. That affectionate look of Śiva was like a refreshing shower of nectar upon the King of Heaven.

content_sanskrit: किरीटकोटिच्युतपारिजात पुष्पोत्करेणानमितेन मूर्ध्ना । स्वर्गैकवन्द्यो जगदेकवन्द्यं तं देवदेवं प्रणनाम देवः ॥

meaning_english: Indra, the foremost among the inhabitants of heaven, bowed his head before Śiva, the supreme Lord of the universe. As he bowed, a shower of Pārijāta flowers fell from the tip of his crown onto the feet of the God of gods.

content_sanskrit: अनेकलोकैकनमस्क्रियार्हं महेश्वरं तं त्रिदशेश्वरः स । भक्त्या नमस्कृत्य कृतार्थतायाः पात्रं पवित्रं परमं बभूव ॥

meaning_english: By bowing with deep devotion to Maheśvara, who is the sole object of worship for all worlds, Indra, the King of the gods, became a supreme and pure vessel of total spiritual fulfillment.

content_sanskrit: सुभक्तिभाजामधि पादपीठं प्रान्तक्षितिं नम्रतरैः शिरोभिः । ततः प्रणेमुः पुरतो गणानां गणाः सुराणां क्रमतः पुरारिम् ॥

meaning_english: Thereafter, the hosts of gods, filled with deep devotion, bowed down in succession before Śiva (the enemy of Pura) in front of His divine attendants, touching the ground near His footstool with their deeply inclined heads.

content_sanskrit: गणोपनीते प्रभुणोपदिष्टः शुभासने हेममये पुरस्तात् । प्रापोपविश्य प्रमुदं सुरेन्द्रः प्रभुप्रसादो हि मुदे न कस्य ॥

meaning_english: Indra, directed by Lord Śiva, sat down on an auspicious golden seat brought by the attendants and experienced great joy. Indeed, who does not feel delighted by the favor shown by the Lord?

content_sanskrit: क्रमेण चान्येऽपि विलोकनेन सम्भाविताः सस्मितमीश्वरेण । उपाविशंस्तोषविशेषमाप्ता दृग्गोचरे तस्य सुराः समग्राः ॥

meaning_english: The other gods were also honored by the Lord in turn with a smiling glance. Attaining a sense of special satisfaction, all the deities sat down within His range of vision.

content_sanskrit: अथाह देवो बलवैरिमुख्यान् गीर्वाणवर्गान्करुणार्द्रचेताः । कृताञ्जलीकान्सुराभिसूतान्ध्वस्तश्रियः श्रान्तमुखानवेक्ष्य ॥

meaning_english: Then, the Lord, His heart melting with compassion, observed the groups of gods headed by Indra. Seeing them with folded hands, their glory vanished and their faces showing exhaustion, He spoke to them.

content_sanskrit: अहो बतानन्तपराक्रमाणां दिवौकसो वीरवरायुधानाम् । हिमोदबिन्दुग्लपितस्य किं यः पद्मस्य दैन्यं दधते मुखानि ॥

meaning_english: O inhabitants of heaven! Have you been displaced from heaven despite your vast store of merit? You still bear the long-carried marks of your own sovereignty, yet you seem to have lost your status.

content_sanskrit: दिवौकसो देवगृहं विहाय मनुष्यसाधारणतामवाप्ताः । यूयं कुतः कारणतश्चरध्वं महीतले मानभृतो महान्तः ॥

meaning_english: O gods! Why do you, who are great and possessed of self-respect, wander on the earth like ordinary humans, having abandoned your divine abode?

content_sanskrit: अनन्यसाधारणसिद्धमुच्चैस्तद्दैवतं धाम निकामरम्यम् । कस्माद कस्मान्निरगाद्भवद्भ्यश्चिरार्जितं पुण्यमिवा पचारात् ॥

meaning_english: Why has that divine abode, which is extraordinarily beautiful, exalted, and uniquely attained, suddenly departed from you, just as long-accumulated merit leaves one due to some sinful lapse?

content_sanskrit: दिवौकसो वो हृदयस्य कस्मात्तयाविधं धैर्यमहार्यमार्याः । अगादगाधस्य जलाशयस्य ग्रीष्मातितापादिवशादिवाम्भः ॥

meaning_english: O noble gods! Why has your unshakeable fortitude left your hearts, much like water disappears from a deep lake due to the intense heat of summer?

content_sanskrit: सुराः सुराधीशपुरःसराणां समीयुषां वः सममातुराणाम् । तद्ब्रूत लोकत्रयजित्वरात्किं महासुरात्तारकतो विरुद्धम् ॥

meaning_english: O gods! All of you, led by Indra, appear equally distressed. Tell me, what harm has been done to you by the great demon Tāraka, the conqueror of the three worlds?

content_sanskrit: पराभवं तस्य महासुरस्य निषेद्धुमेकोऽहमलम्भविष्णुः । दावानलप्लोषविपत्तिमन्यो महाम्बुदात्किं हरते वनानाम् ॥

meaning_english: Lord Śiva declares that he alone is capable of thwarting the defeat caused by that great demon Tāraka. He uses a metaphor, asking who else besides a massive rain-cloud can remove the calamity of a forest fire that scorches the woods.

content_sanskrit: इतीरिते मन्मथमर्दनेन सुराः सुरेन्द्रप्रमुखा मुखेषु । सान्द्रप्रमोदाश्रुतरङ्गितेषु दधुः श्रियं सत्वरमाश्वसन्तः ॥

meaning_english: When Lord Śiva, the destroyer of Kāmadeva, spoke these words, the gods led by Indra quickly took heart. Their faces, rippling with tears of intense joy, regained their natural splendor and grace.

content_sanskrit: ततो गिरीशस्य गिरां विरामे जगाद लब्धेऽवसरे सुरेन्द्रः । भवन्ति वाचोऽवसरे प्रयुक्ता ध्रुवं फलाविष्टमहोदयाय ॥

meaning_english: Then, as Śiva finished speaking and an opportunity arose, Indra spoke. He noted that words uttered at the right moment certainly lead to a great and successful outcome.

meaning_english: Indra addresses Śiva as the All-knowing One, stating that through the eternal lamp of his knowledge—which dispels the darkness of ignorance and possesses unfailing light—everything in the past, present, and future is visible to him.

content_sanskrit: दुर्वारदोरुद्यमदुःसहेन यत्तारकेणामरघस्मरेण । तदीशतामाप्तवता निरस्ता वयं दिवोऽमी वद किं न वेत्सि ॥

meaning_english: Indra asks Śiva if he is not aware that they have been expelled from heaven by Tāraka. He describes the demon as a devourer of gods who attained lordship through the unbearable strength and unstoppable effort of his arms.

content_sanskrit: विधेरमोघं स वरप्रसादमासाद्य सद्यस्त्रिजगज्जिगीषुः । सुरानशेषानहकप्रमुख्यान्दोर्दण्डचण्डो मनुते तृणाय ॥

meaning_english: Having obtained an unfailing boon from Brahmā, Tāraka became instantly intent on conquering the three worlds. Fierce with his powerful arms, he now considers all the gods, including the Sun-god, as insignificant as a blade of grass.

content_sanskrit: स्तुत्या पुरास्माभिरुपासितेन पितामहेनेति निरुपितं नः । सेनापतिः संयति दैत्यमेतं पुरः स्मरारातिसुतो निहन्ति ॥

meaning_english: Indra recalls that when they worshipped Brahmā with praises in the past, he prophesied that the son of Lord Śiva (the enemy of Kāmadeva) would become their commander-in-chief and slay this demon in battle.

content_sanskrit: अहो ततोऽनन्तरमद्ययाव त्सुदुःसहां तस्य पराभवार्तिम् । विषेहिरे हन्त हृदन्तशल्यमाज्ञानिवेशं त्रिदिवौकसौऽमी ॥

meaning_english: Indra laments that from that time until today, the gods have been forced to endure the unbearable pain of defeat. They have suffered his commands like a painful thorn lodged deep within their hearts.

content_sanskrit: निदाघधामक्लमविक्लवानां नवीनमम्भोदमिवौषधीनाम् । सुनन्दनं नन्दनमात्मनो नः सेनान्यमेतं स्वयमादिश त्वम् ॥

meaning_english: Indra requests Śiva to personally appoint his son as their commander. He likens this act to a fresh rain-cloud appearing for plants withered by the scorching summer sun, bringing them relief and great joy.

content_sanskrit: त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्मीहृदयैकशल्यं समूलमुत्खाय महासुरं तम् । अस्माकमेषां पुरतो भवन्स दुःखापहारं युधि यो विधत्ते ॥
padaccheda: त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्मीहृदयैकशल्यम् । समूलम् । उत्खाय । महासुरम् । तम् । अस्माकम् । एषाम् । पुरतः । भवन् । सः । दुःखापहारम् । युधि । यः । विधत्ते
anvaya: यः युधि त्रैलोक्यलक्ष्मीहृदयैकशल्यम् तम् महासुरम् समूलम् उत्खाय पुरतः भवन् अस्माकम् एषाम् दुःखापहारम् विधत्ते।
meaning_english: Indra emphasizes that Śiva's son, by leading them in battle, will uproot that great demon who is like a thorn in the heart of the three worlds' prosperity. By doing so, he will finally bring about the complete removal of the gods' sorrows.

content_sanskrit: महाहवे नाथ तवास्य सूनोः शस्त्रैः शितैः कृत्तशिरोधराणाम् । महासुराणां रमणीविलोपैर्दिशो दशैता मुखरीभवन्तु ॥
padaccheda: महाहवे । नाथ । तव । अस्य । सूनोः । शस्त्रैः । शितैः । कृत्तशिरोधराणाम् । महासुराणाम् । रमणीविलोपैः । दिशः । दश । एताः । मुखरीभवन्तु
anvaya: नाथ तव अस्य सूनोः शितैः शस्त्रैः कृत्तशिरोधराणाम् महासुराणां रमणीविलोपैः एताः दश दिशः मुखरीभवन्तु ॥
meaning_english: Indra prays to Śiva, saying that in the great battle, let the ten directions resound with the wailing of the wives of the great demons whose necks will be severed by the sharp weapons of Śiva's son, Kārttikeya.

content_sanskrit: महारणक्षोणिपशूपहारीकृतेऽसुरे तत्र तवात्मजेन । बन्दिस्थितानां सुदृशां करोतु वेणिप्रमोक्षं सुरलोक एषः ॥

meaning_english: Indra continues, expressing hope that when the demon Tāraka is sacrificed like an animal on the battlefield by Śiva's son, the inhabitants of heaven may finally untie the braids of the beautiful captive women, signaling their liberation.

content_sanskrit: इत्थं सुरेन्द्रे वदति स्मरारिः सुरारिदुश्चेष्टितजातरोषः । कृतानुकम्पस्त्रिदशेषु तेषु भूयोऽपि भूताधिपतिर्बभाषे ॥

meaning_english: As Indra spoke thus, Śiva (the lord of beings), whose anger was provoked by the wicked deeds of the demons but who felt compassion for the gods, spoke once again.

content_sanskrit: अहो अहो देवगणाः सुरेन्द्रमुख्याः शृणुध्वं वचनं ममैते । विचेष्टते शङ्कर एष देवः कार्याय सज्जो भवतां सुताद्यैः ॥

meaning_english: Śiva addressed the gods, led by Indra, asking them to listen to his words. He stated that he is ready for the task and is acting through his son and others for their benefit.

content_sanskrit: पुरा मयाकारि गिरीन्द्रपुत्र्याः प्रतिग्रहोऽयं नियतात्मनापि । तत्रैष हेतुः खलु तद्भवेन वीरेण यद्वध्यत एष शत्रुः ॥
padaccheda: पुरा । मया । अकारि । गिरीन्द्रपुत्र्याः । प्रतिग्रहः । अयम् । नियतात्मना । अपि । तत्र । एषः । हेतुः । खलु । तद्भवेन । वीरेण । यद् । वध्यते । एष । शत्रुः

meaning_english: Śiva explains that although he is self-controlled, he accepted Pārvatī only for this reason: that the heroic son born of her would be the one to slay this enemy (Tāraka).

content_sanskrit: अत्रोपपन्नं तदमी नियुज्य कुमारमेनं पृतनापतित्वे । निघ्नन्तु शत्रुं सुरलोकमेष भुनक्तु भूयोऽपि सुरैः सहेन्द्रः ॥

meaning_english: Śiva suggests that it is appropriate for the gods to appoint Kumāra as the commander of the army to destroy the enemy, so that Indra may once again rule over heaven along with the other deities.

content_sanskrit: इत्युदीर्य भगवांस्तमात्मजं घोरसङ्गरमहोत्सवोत्सुकम् । नन्दनं हि जहि देवविद्विषं संयतीति निजगाद शङ्करः ॥

meaning_english: Having said this, Lord Śiva spoke to his son Kumāra, who was eager for the great 'festival' of the terrible battle, saying, "O son, slay the enemy of the gods in battle."

content_sanskrit: शासनं पशुपतेः स कुमार स्वीचकार शिरसावनतेन । सर्वथैव पितृभक्तिरतानामेष एव परमः खलु धर्मः ॥

meaning_english: Kumāra accepted Śiva's command with a bowed head; indeed, for those devoted to their father, following his command is the highest duty.

content_sanskrit: असुरयुद्धविधौ विबुधेश्वरे पशुपतौ वदतीति तवात्मजम् । गिरिजया मुमुदे सुतविक्रमे सति न नन्दति का खलु वीरसूः ॥

meaning_english: When Śiva spoke thus regarding the war with the demons, Pārvatī rejoiced in the prowess of her son. Indeed, what mother of a hero would not feel joy in her son's valor?

content_sanskrit: सुरपरिवृढः प्रौढं वीरं कुमारमुमापतेर्बलवदमरारातिस्त्रीणां दृगञ्जनभञ्जनम् । जगदभयदं सद्यः प्राप्य प्रमोदपरोऽभवद्ध्रुवमभिमते पूर्णे को वा मुदा न हि माद्यति ॥
padaccheda: सुरपरिवृढः । प्रौढम् । वीरम् । कुमारम् । उमापतेः । बलवदमरारातिस्त्रीणाम् । दृगञ्जनभञ्जनम् । जगदभयदम् । सद्यः । प्राप्य । प्रमोदपरः । अभवत् । ध्रुवम् । अभिमते । पूर्णे । कः । वा । मुदा । न । हि । माद्यति
anvaya: सुरपरिवृढः उमापतेः प्रौढम् वीरम् जगदभयदम् अमरारातिस्त्रीणां दृगञ्जनभञ्जनम् एनम् कुमारम् सद्यः प्राप्य प्रमोदपरः अभवत् अभिमते पूर्णे सति को वा मुदा न माद्यति ॥
meaning_english: Indra, the leader of the gods, became exceedingly joyful upon receiving Kumāra—the mighty son of Śiva who gives fearlessness to the world and causes the wives of demons to weep. Truly, who would not be intoxicated with joy when their heart's desire is fulfilled?
